highlights.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
highlights.summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China.
body: Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going.

According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.

As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

highlights.title: Eagles sink Cowboys with historic NFL Thanksgiving comeback
highlights.summary: Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left as the Philadelphia Eagles produced a staggering 21-point comeback to beat the Dallas Cowboys 39-38 in a Thanksgiving epic on Thursday.
body: Joe Milton throws three touchdown passes while DeVonta Smith records 200 receiving yards as the Philadelphia Eagles deliver the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving Day history to shock the Dallas Cowboys in a 39-38 victory.

Dallas had led by as many as 21 points in the third quarter only to see ever-reliable kicker Brandon Aubrey miss a 40-yard field goal before the Eagles pulled to within two, down 38-36 with two minutes remaining.

Dak Prescott was then sacked by Ty Johnson on fourth-and-one with 55 seconds left before Markquese Bell gifted the Eagles a first down with a pass interference penalty on third-and-one on the ensuing possession.
It would eventually tee up Elliott's crowning moment as he kicked the Eagles to the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history.

highlights.title: PS1 and Xbox Hallmark Christmas Ornaments Are on Sale for Black Friday
highlights.summary: If you’re a gamer of a certain age, you may have fond memories of playing the original PlayStation or Xbox consoles. Now you can get gorgeously rendered tiny versions of both classic systems in the form of Christmas ornaments from Hallmark’s Keepsake line.
body: The original PlayStation came out in the US in 1994 and has been getting a decent amount of attention lately. LEGO recently turned it into a near 1:1 scale buildable set that I reviewed. This Hallmark ornament PS1 is even closer to the real thing (though much smaller). It’s highly detailed and just beautifully made. When you press the power button the little green light flashes and it plays the iconic PS1 startup sound. The Amazon listing has a video of it. Check it out.

The Xbox is just as authentically detailed as the PlayStation. It depicts Microsoft’s black-and-green machine, complete with a Duke controller. Press the power button, and the circle on the front lights up, and it plays the startup sound, followed by the opening music from Halo: Combat Evolved. You can see a video of the process on the Amazon listing.

The PS1 normally sells for $29.99, but it’s on sale for $18.80 for Black Friday. That’s only a few cents higher than the all-time low price, not enough to worry about. The Xbox has an MSRP of $27.99, but it’s on sale for $19.60. That’s a new all-time low price.

highlights.title: Supercell shooter Boat Game is back in limited testing
highlights.summary: The Finnish firm’s lowkey shooter appears to be back on the App Store and Google Play in the US, Canada, Mexico, Malaysia and the Philippines.
body: Supercell appears to have revamped its looter shooter Boat Game and is now testing the title with a limited number of players.
The game was last seen back in October 2025, when Supercell ran a second alpha test. It was first revealed in February 2025, when selected players were part of a first alpha test.
When it first emerged Boat Game appeared to be more of a Sea of Thieves-like game, but the new edition is described as an extraction shooter on its app store listings.

A reported Discord message from Supercell’s community team reads: “The reception to the game last year was not what we hoped and we’ve spent this year thinking hard about what experience we want to give players and putting those ideas into the game.”

highlights.title: Why is there a shortage of 'wizard' elevator mechanics?
highlights.summary: The pay is good and there's lots of work, so what's behind the shortage of elevator mechanics?
body: Some of them are angry. Nerves are frayed. Many of them are just relieved that he's here.

When a lift stops working in Chicago, frazzled building managers might get a visit from Jim Lembesis. For more than 47 years, Lembesis has repaired and upgraded lifts. He says he understands why staff and residents are so anxious to have things working again.
"They wait and they wait," says Lembesis, a field technician for Parkway Elevators. "There's a lot of frustration. Sometimes it's a repeat issue. It's a never-ending cycle, you know what I mean?"

The widely reported shortage of lift and escalator mechanics in the US, which is also a problem in many other countries, has got worse over time, he adds: "It's been like night and day compared to when I started."

highlights.title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
highlights.summary: The FCA warned against “another force of attack” from agents after the company declined a request to work on joint testing ahead of rolling out its personal agent in the UK on Tuesday.
body: Meta declined a suggestion from the UK’s financial regulator last week that they joint-test Muse using their sandbox, according to the watchdog’s head of innovation Colin Payne. It comes as regulators across the UK, including the competition and data watchdogs, warned Meta it needs to ensure its AI products comply with UK consumer protection laws.

“It’s another force of attack, agents hitting the streets, most of them coming from the US,” Payne, of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), said Tuesday in a panel hosted by AI firm Whitespace. “We’ve got a number of entrants into the market. We want to see what they’re going to be doing in the market. I think it’s just reasonable,” he later explained to WIRED. Payne told WIRED the FCA had been hoping the organizations could work together to investigate what interactions might look like between the tool, marketed as a personal assistant, and a normal customer.
His organization has been experimenting with other firms as many, including Amazon, roll out AI shopping assistants, and other agentic tools in the UK.

highlights.title: After Playing Infinity Nikki 3.0 for Four Hours, its New Cities and Outfits Are Just Some of the Additions Worth Returning For
highlights.summary: The new 3.0 update has tons of new stuff to explore including new locations, outfits and gameplay systems, although don't expect any kind of proper challenge.
body: When Infinity Nikki first launched in 2024, it introduced players around the world to the dress-up world of mobile game star Nikki in her first 3D console/PC adventure, an open world filled with wholesome fun, fashion and friendship. 2025’s V2.0 update introduced a new area to the world of Miraland, as well as new ways to traverse it. But now with the new V3.0 update titled Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, Nikki’s wonderful world has been expanded significantly – with its richest locations yet, and even a cute convertible to traverse it with.

To give you an idea of how huge this update is, I played for over four hours at developer Infold’s Shanghai office, focusing mainly on story content and with only the slightest bit of open-world exploration and lifestyle simulation gameplay, and didn't even see all of one of its two new cities. The golden path apparently offers some nine hours of story content, with two dense and exciting new areas to get lost in. Between the V3.0 launch and Nikki’s birthday celebration campaign, players can get 160 free draws and 19 new sets of clothing.

highlights.title: Asia made a big AI bet on Nvidia. What happens now?
highlights.summary: Asian stocks have been on a rollercoaster ride after Jensen Huang's shock return as Nvidia CEO.
body: Jensen Huang's extraordinary return as Nvidia's boss rocked not only its shares in New York but also sent shockwaves through the artificial intelligence (AI) industry around the world.
Those jolts were felt particularly in Asia as the saga highlighted the region's huge exposure to the technology.

Tech-heavy stock indexes in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan went on a rollercoaster ride this week. Markets soared after a near-trillion dollar surge in Nvidia's share price but then slumped as concerns about political and regulatory scrutiny hit investor confidence.

The chipmaker is a "symbolic bellwether" of the AI trade that is fast becoming key to places like South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Malaysia," says Dylan Loh, an international studies lecturer at Nanyang Technological University.

highlights.title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
highlights.summary: On the same day that Anthropic entered the public market, a painstakingly human video game became one of most successful entertainment launches of all time.
body: It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week.

GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ( $2.9 billion ) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ( $2 billion ).
The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI.

Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda, who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.”

highlights.title: Star Trek: Voyager Officially Revisits the Series' Best Two-Parter in a Brand-New Way
highlights.summary: One of the best two-episode arcs in Star Trek: Voyager, if not the entire Star Trek franchise, is the "Year of Hell" duology. The story from the show's fourth season pitted the crew of Voyager against a unique threat that tested their perseverance more than any previous enemy had.
body: Daedalic Entertainment has announced that the fourth Expansion Pass DLC for Across the Unknown will be inspired by "Year of Hell". The announcement describes the DLC as "a self-contained mini-campaign of three new sectors." The DLC will be released on Dec. 9. As in the show​​​​​​​, the game will pit players against the Krenim captain Annorax as he wields a weapon that allows him to alter history and destroy entire species. As a standalone expansion, Year of Hell won't affect any of players' main-game save files​​​​​​​.

Unlike the base game, which sees the Voyager trying to rebuild​​​​​​​ and survive with few resources, Year of Hell will invert the traditional gameplay experience. Players will start with a fully repaired and fully equipped ship​​​​​​​ before encountering the Krenim. While damaged rooms will be repairable, lost decks will cause players to lose every room, and players can lose up to five decks​​​​​​​. Crew members can also die, leaving the Voyager crew scrambling to stay alive​​​​​​​. Daedalic Entertainment says that the goal of the DLC "isn't to finish with a perfect ship. It's to see how many of your crew are still standing after twelve months."

highlights.title: ‘Not really the thing to take a victory lap in’: the meaning of Jensen Huang’s new jacket
highlights.summary: Nvidia’s boss has returned in a new uniform. But what does swapping leather for cotton say about power and leadership? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here. It’s been a big week for the stock market and the leather jacket-wearing community.
body: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, who had resigned as chief executive of the chipmaker after reports of multiple affairs, was reinstated as CEO. But as he returned to the company’s Silicon Valley headquarters surrounded by clapping employees chanting his name, one thing was amiss. Jensen was back, but the black leather jacket that had been his trademark piece for nearly two decades remained absent from its former power position. In its place? A navy cotton jacket.

In his first post-return company all-hands meeting, Huang apologised to employees, telling them he had made some “terrible mistakes”. He also said: “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around … I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”

What better than a humble cotton jacket to emphasise Huang’s newfound morality? A leather jacket comes with in-built bravado. It walks a fine line between confident and cocky, whereas its cotton cousin is much more subtle. It suggests modesty and restraint.
“I changed my jacket. I’m different now,” read one comment below a photo of a leather-less Huang. “Someone in fashion needs to make ‘The Jensen’ jacket right now,” read another.

highlights.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
highlights.summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off "the private chat histories of more…
body: A bipartisan coalition of AGs say Character.AI is planning to sell the personal data of minors to the highest bidder.

In October, Character.AI filed for bankruptcy following years of scandals and legal challenges, including from Disney. Disney ended up buying some of the company’s assets and hiring its CEO, Karandeep Anand, in a sort of “acquihire” arrangement that will also see “a number of Character.AI’s technical team” join the entertainment giant. The Disney deal also faced opposition from a similarly broad coalition of AGs.

The main point of contention with Character.AI’s plan to sell its chat data is that it offers no protections for users. The AGs say there are no requirements that the buyer honor existing privacy policies, no avenues for users to delete their data, and no inherent limits on what a buyer could do with that data, including selling it on to yet another party. It doesn’t help that the first bidder has a limited paper trail, having only been established on November 13th, 2026, with no parent company or investors listed.

highlights.title: Mammy Goose is well and truly cooked in Glasgow’s incredibly random Aladdin
highlights.summary: King’s theatre, Glasgow The offensive stereotypes have been ditched but this glitzy panto starring Elaine C Smith shoehorns in plenty of irrelevant material. Staging a traditional Aladdin in 2026 is problematic.
body: Stereotypes aside, Aladdin can still be a gripping coming-of-age story about greed and gullibility, poverty and power. The stakes can be loaded with deceit, jeopardy and cunning. In this version, set in the land of Pantomania, almost none of that survives.

Here, Widow Twankey has morphed into Mammy Goose (Elaine C Smith), inexplicably the proprietor of an ailing theatre. This is located near a haunted castle which, just as inexplicably, contains a panto hall of fame. Nice to see the portraits of previous King’s stars on display, but it is as irrelevant to the plot as the ballet moves of Priscilla the Goose (Oliver Moriarty), who is shoehorned into the action like so much else.

Just as extraneous are a tedious set-piece sketch involving the names of television programmes and a standard-issue haunted bedroom routine, complete with scripted ad-libs. With so much irrelevant material, the cave and the magic lamp seem like afterthoughts. So too does the featureless romance between Aladdin (Johnny Mac) and Princess Jemima (Blythe Jandoo), who scarcely get a chance to speak – let alone fall in love.

highlights.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
highlights.summary: A Blog post by ggml-org on Hugging Face
body: The llama.cpp × AMD Benchmark dashboard is available on Hugging Face. It lets you track prompt processing and text generation performance across llama.cpp builds, models, and quantizations, so you can explore how local inference performs on AMD Ryzen and Radeon hardware.

Local inference performance changes as models, kernels, and builds evolve. We want those changes to be easy to inspect for any AMD developer: pick a hardware, a model and a build, compare quantizations, and follow performance over time. The benchmark workflow and underlying results are public, so you can also inspect how we benchmark inference performance.
You can choose Hardware, Model, and llama.cpp build in the Configuration sidebar. The current hardware choices are Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) and Radeon AI Pro R9700S (gfx1201).

Both tests start at context depth zero ( n_depth=0 ). PP512 measures processing 512 input tokens without generation; TG128 measures generating 128 tokens without a pre-existing context. The plotted value is the mean throughput ( avg_ts ). These are useful reference workloads, while the Context scaling tab lets you explore token generation throughput as the context grows.

You can chalk this up to a little Thanksgiving homesickness, as I wasn’t able to travel to my home state for the holiday, but I am convinced I am on to something here.

The thing that really makes GTA 6 so special is Leonida. Rockstar’s digital recreation of Florida is a perfect playground for GTA’s sandbox chaos, and it takes advantage of the state’s geographical diversity to do that. You’ve got a bustling Miami to build on for Vice City, but you also have a mix of run-down towns, rural farmlands, beaches, and quiet islands. That wide array of locations makes for a more varied GTA experience, as you bounce between areas with very different speeds.

highlights.title: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again
highlights.summary: Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success.
body: “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.”

Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura.

highlights.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
highlights.summary: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users.
body: Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.

First spotted by Patentlyze, the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers.
